about: Bible twenty questions: the model passes' values (design §5.3-§5.4), merged by tq_merge.py. Not hand-edited. by: model (passes agree), resolved (the resolver settled a yes-against-no), unresolved (dispute pending; unsure), rule (a yes broke implies/excludes; unsure), single-pass / missing-pass (a pass had no usable answer).

queen.why: Jacob is a man; no verse gives him a queen role.

high-priest.why: Nothing in the text gives Jacob the high priest role.

warrior.why: Jacob never fights or commands an army; he prepares for Esau with gifts and prayer.

levite.why: Jacob is Levi's father; no verse states Jacob's own tribe.

court-official.why: Jacob serves Laban as a herdsman, not a king's court official.

shepherd.why: Jacob says he will again feed and keep Laban's flock.

fisherman.why: Nothing in the text gives Jacob the work of a fisherman.

twin.why: Born the younger of Isaac and Rebekah's twins, grasping Esau's heel.

name-changed.why: God says his name will no longer be Jacob but Israel.

miracle-birth.why: Rebekah was barren; the LORD answered Isaac's prayer and she conceived the twins.

long-life.why: Jacob's life was 147 years.

tribe-judah.why: Jacob is the patriarch; no verse states his own tribe.

tribe-benjamin.why: Jacob is the patriarch; no verse states his own tribe.

raised.why: Jacob dies and is buried in Machpelah; no return to life.

taken-up.why: Jacob dies and his sons bury him in the cave of Machpelah.

angel.why: The angel of God speaks to Jacob in a dream.

dream.why: Jacob dreams of a ladder to heaven with the LORD above it.

interpret-dreams.why: Jacob reports his own dreams; he never explains anyone else's dream.

prison.why: Jacob is never imprisoned or carried off captive.

killed.why: Jacob breathes his last and is gathered to his people; not killed.

battle.why: Jacob takes no part in a battle; Simeon and Levi attack Shechem.

enemy.why: Jacob is part of God's people; he does not fight against them.

betrayed.why: He deceives blind Isaac and Esau; whether that counts as betrayal is open.

anointed.why: He anoints a pillar at Bethel; he himself is never anointed with oil.

built.why: Jacob builds an altar at Bethel, called El-bethel.

water-miracle.why: He crosses the Jabbok ford by ordinary means, not on dry ground by miracle.

song.why: No psalm or song in Scripture is credited to Jacob.

young.why: Birthright bargain and blessing are not dated to childhood; ages not given.

egypt.why: Jacob lives in the land of Egypt seventeen years before his death.

babylon.why: He lives in Haran and Canaan; no Babylon or Persia.

jerusalem.why: He lives at Shechem and Hebron; no Jerusalem.

galilee.why: Nothing places Jacob in Galilee.

sea.why: Jacob travels by land and never sails by ship.

in-law.why: Named in Exodus to Deuteronomy as Israel's father; not shown acting there.

in-joshua-ruth.why: Only mentioned in Joshua and Ruth; no action by him there.

in-samuel-kings.why: Only mentioned in Samuel and Kings; he does not act there.

in-1-kings.why: Only mentioned in 1 Kings (Elijah's altar stones); he does not act.

in-2-kings.why: Only mentioned in 2 Kings; he does not act there.

in-chronicles.why: Only named in genealogies in Chronicles; no action by him.

in-ezra-esther.why: Only mentioned in Ezra and Nehemiah; no action by him there.

in-prophets.why: Named by the prophets as a people or patriarch; he does not act there.

in-poetry.why: Named in Psalms as a people; he is not credited with words.

in-gospels.why: Named in genealogy and John 4 well; he does not act in the Gospels.

in-letters.why: Hebrews 11:21 cites his blessing as faith; he does not write, receive or get greeted.

in-revelation.why: Only the tribes named after him appear; Jacob himself does not act.

ruler.why: Judah never reigns; his story is family and Egypt, not kingship.

ruler-israel.why: Judah never rules Israel or Judah; the kings are his descendants, not him.

ruler-foreign.why: No rule over any nation other than Israel is given to Judah.

queen.why: Judah is a man, not a queen.

high-priest.why: No priestly office is given to Judah; Genesis 49 gives him kingship blessing, not priesthood.

warrior.why: No soldiering or command is described for Judah personally.

court-official.why: Judah pleads before Joseph, but he holds no court office under a king.

shepherd.why: Judah has sheep and sheepshearers at Timnah, so he keeps flocks.

fisherman.why: Judah is never a fisherman.

name-changed.why: Leah names Judah at birth; no later new name is given.

miracle-birth.why: Leah had already borne three sons before Judah, so she was not barren until his birth.

long-life.why: Judah's age at death is not given in the text.

miracles.why: No miracle is worked through Judah.

raised.why: Judah does not die and return to life; his sons Er and Onan die.

taken-up.why: Judah dies in Scripture's account; he is not taken up to God.

angel.why: No angel speaks to Judah in the text.

dream.why: No dream or vision from God is given to Judah.

interpret-dreams.why: Judah explains no one's dream.

prison.why: Judah offers to become a bondman in Benjamin's place but is never imprisoned or captive.

killed.why: Judah is not put to death by anyone.

battle.why: Judah takes no part in any battle described in the text.

enemy.why: Judah proposes selling Joseph, a member of Israel's family; whether this counts as opposing God's pe

anointed.why: No anointing with oil is given to Judah.

built.why: Judah builds no structure described in Scripture.

animal.why: The young goat in Genesis 38 is livestock in passing, not the centre of his story.

water-miracle.why: Judah does not cross water by miracle or walk on water.

song.why: No psalm or song is credited to Judah by name.

young.why: No childhood or youthful deed of Judah is recorded.

egypt.why: Judah goes down to Egypt with the family and is sent ahead to Joseph in Goshen.

babylon.why: Judah never lives in Babylon or Persia.

jerusalem.why: Judah lives in Canaan and Egypt, not in Jerusalem.

galilee.why: Judah never lives or works in Galilee.

sea.why: Judah makes no journey by ship.

in-law.why: Judah is only listed or blessed in Exodus to Deuteronomy, not shown acting there.

in-joshua-ruth.why: Judah appears in Joshua, Judges and Ruth only as a tribe or land, not as an actor.

in-samuel-kings.why: Judah appears in Samuel and Kings as the tribe or kingdom, not as an actor.

in-1-kings.why: 1 Kings names Judah as tribe and kingdom, not Judah acting.

in-2-kings.why: 2 Kings names Judah as kingdom and people, not Judah acting.

in-chronicles.why: Chronicles lists Judah as a son and tribe; no event shows him acting.

in-ezra-esther.why: Ezra to Esther name Judah as people or land, not as an actor.

in-prophets.why: Prophets name Judah as kingdom and people; Judah himself is not an actor.

in-poetry.why: Psalms name Judah as tribe or kingdom, not as a speaking or acting person.

in-gospels.why: Judah appears only in Matthew 1:2 and Luke's genealogy, not in acting events.

in-letters.why: Hebrews 7:14 mentions Judah as a tribe; he neither writes, receives nor is greeted.

in-revelation.why: Revelation 5:5 names the tribe of Judah, not Judah acting.

era-judges.why: David's story is in the united monarchy, after Saul began to reign, not in the judges' era.

era-divided.why: David died before the kingdom split; his reign ended before Rehoboam.

queen.why: David is a man and was never a queen.

high-priest.why: Nothing in the text gives David the office of high priest; priests like Abiathar serve him.

warrior.why: Saul set David over the men of war, and he fought as a soldier and commander.

court-official.why: David entered Saul's service at court as a harp player and armourbearer.

shepherd.why: David says he had been tending his father's sheep.

fisherman.why: David is never shown working as a fisherman.

twin.why: Scripture does not say whether David had a twin.

name-changed.why: Scripture does not give David a new name; his name stays the same.

miracle-birth.why: David's mother is never named, so her fertility history is not given.

long-life.why: David's age at death is not given as a number; he dies in a good old age.

raised.why: David dies and is buried; he is not raised back to life.

taken-up.why: David dies and is buried in the city of David; he is not taken to heaven.

angel.why: The angel of the LORD speaks to Gad to tell David; direct speech to David is unclear.

dream.why: He sees the angel awake in 1 Chronicles 21:16; not clearly a dream or vision from God.

interpret-dreams.why: David is never shown explaining the meaning of a dream.

prison.why: David flees from Saul but is not imprisoned or carried off captive.

killed.why: David dies and rests with his fathers, not killed by others.

leader.why: The LORD tells David he will shepherd Israel and be ruler over Israel as a whole.

battle.why: David and his men go to Keilah, fight the Philistines and strike them with a mighty blow.

enemy.why: He fought Saul's house in a civil war, but he is God's chosen king, so readers could differ.

anointed.why: Samuel anoints David with horn of oil in the presence of his brothers.

built.why: David builds up the city of Zion all the way around, making its walls and terraces.

water-miracle.why: David never crosses water on dry ground or walks on water.

song.why: Psalm 3 is credited to David by name, as a psalm of David.

young.why: As a youth David kills Goliath; Goliath despises him because he is just a boy.

egypt.why: David is never shown living or working in Egypt.

babylon.why: David is never shown living in Babylon or Persia.

jerusalem.why: David captures the fortress of Zion and takes up residence there as the City of David.

galilee.why: David's story is set in Judah, Hebron, Jerusalem and the wilderness, not Galilee.

sea.why: David is never shown travelling by ship.

in-joshua-ruth.why: David is only named in Ruth's genealogy, not taking part in its events.

in-ezra-esther.why: David is only mentioned in Ezra as the king who prescribed or appointed things.

in-prophets.why: David is mentioned in the prophets, often as a title or a promise, not acting in their events.

in-poetry.why: David is credited with the words of Psalm 3 and other psalms.

in-gospels.why: David appears in the Gospels as quoted or referenced, such as Mark 2:25 and the genealogy.

in-letters.why: David is quoted in Romans and Hebrews; it is open whether that counts as writing or receiving.

in-revelation.why: David appears only as the Root of David title in Revelation, not acting in its events.

era-conquest.why: Joshua 1:1 says the LORD spoke to Joshua after the death of Moses; Moses died before the conquest.

ruler.why: Moses never reigns as king, queen or pharaoh; he leads and judges but rules no kingdom.

ruler-israel.why: Moses is never king of Israel or Judah; he leads the people as prophet and mediator.

ruler-foreign.why: No nation other than Israel is ruled by Moses; he is not a pharaoh or foreign king.

queen.why: Moses is a man and not a queen.

priest.why: Psalm 99:6 names Moses and Aaron as among the LORD's priests.

high-priest.why: Aaron is high priest; Moses is never called high priest.

judge.why: Moses judged before the period of Israel's judges; he is not one of the judges after Joshua.

warrior.why: Moses sends the thousand from each tribe into battle, commanding the army.

court-official.why: Nothing gives Moses a role as an official or servant at Pharaoh's court.

shepherd.why: Moses was tending the flock of Jethro his father-in-law.

fisherman.why: Moses is never a fisherman.

twin.why: Scripture does not say whether Moses had a twin.

name-changed.why: Pharaoh's daughter named him; she is not God, a king or Jesus.

miracle-birth.why: Scripture does not say whether his mother was barren before he was born.

long-life.why: Deuteronomy 34:7 says Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died.

miracles.why: The LORD did as Moses requested and the frogs died, a miracle through Moses.

taken-up.why: Deuteronomy 34:5 says Moses the servant of the LORD died in Moab.

angel.why: Acts 7:38 speaks of the angel who spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.

interpret-dreams.why: Moses is never said to explain the meaning of a dream.

prison.why: Moses flees Egypt and is never imprisoned or taken captive.

killed.why: Moses dies in Moab; he is not put to death by others.

leader.why: Psalm 77:20 says God led His people by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

battle.why: Moses sends the army into battle against Midian, acting as commander.

enemy.why: Moses opposes Pharaoh, not God's people; the opposition to Moses comes from others.

betrayed.why: Moses never betrays or denies someone close to him.

anointed.why: Moses anoints Aaron and his sons; nothing says Moses himself was anointed with oil.

built.why: The tent of meeting is described as the tabernacle Moses had made in the wilderness.

water-miracle.why: Moses stretches out his hand and the waters are divided so Israel crosses on dry ground.

song.why: Revelation 15:3 credits the song sung to God as the song of God's servant Moses.

young.why: Scripture tells of no act of his own while a child or youth; his grown-up deeds come later.

egypt.why: Moses grows up in Pharaoh's household in Egypt and becomes Pharaoh's daughter's son.

babylon.why: Moses never lives in Babylon or Persia.

jerusalem.why: Moses never lives or works in Jerusalem.

galilee.why: Moses never lives or works in Galilee.

sea.why: Moses makes no journey by ship; he crosses the sea on dry ground.

in-joshua-ruth.why: Moses appears in Joshua and Judges only as mentioned or recalled, not acting in those events.

in-samuel-kings.why: Moses appears in Samuel and Kings only by mention or quotation, not as a participant.

in-1-kings.why: Moses is only mentioned in 1 Kings, such as the Law of Moses, not acting there.

in-2-kings.why: Moses is only mentioned in 2 Kings, such as the Book of the Law of Moses.

in-chronicles.why: Moses is named in Chronicles only in genealogy and references to the Law, not acting there.

in-ezra-esther.why: Moses is only mentioned in Ezra and Nehemiah through the Law, not as a participant.

in-prophets.why: Moses is only mentioned in the prophets, such as Isaiah 63 and Jeremiah 15, not acting in them.

in-poetry.why: Psalm 90 is credited with words of Moses the man of God in its superscription.

in-gospels.why: Moses appears at the Transfiguration, talking with Jesus and Elijah.

in-letters.why: Moses is only mentioned in the letters, such as Hebrews 3:2 and 2 Corinthians 3, not writing or gree

in-revelation.why: Revelation 15:3 names the song of Moses, but Moses himself is not shown acting in the book.

era-conquest.why: Aaron died at Mount Hor and never entered Canaan, before the conquest under Joshua.

queen.why: Nothing in the text gives Aaron a queen's role.

high-priest.why: Called Aaron the chief priest; anointed as the first priest.

warrior.why: No soldiering or army command is given to Aaron.

court-official.why: He speaks to Pharaoh as an envoy, not as an official serving a king's court.

shepherd.why: No flock-keeping is ascribed to Aaron; Psalm 77:20 is only a metaphor.

fisherman.why: No fishing appears in his story.

twin.why: Twin birth is not stated for Aaron.

name-changed.why: No new name is given to Aaron in the text.

long-life.why: Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.

miracles.why: Aaron stretched out his hand and the frogs came up over Egypt.

raised.why: Aaron dies on Mount Hor and does not return to life.

taken-up.why: Aaron dies on Mount Hor; he is not taken up alive.

angel.why: The LORD speaks to Aaron directly; no angel speaks to him.

interpret-dreams.why: No dream interpretation is ascribed to Aaron.

prison.why: Aaron is never imprisoned or taken captive.

killed.why: Aaron dies on the mountain; no one kills him.

leader.why: God led His people by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

battle.why: Aaron takes part in no battle.

betrayed.why: He spoke against Moses with Miriam, but no clear betrayal or denial is stated.

anointed.why: Moses poured the anointing oil on Aaron's head.

built.why: He made the golden calf and an altar, but not a famous structure like the tabernacle.

animal.why: The rod turns into a serpent, but the serpent is not clearly the centre of his story.

water-miracle.why: Aaron crosses no sea or river on dry ground and walks on no water.

song.why: No psalm or song is credited to Aaron by name.

young.why: No childhood or youthful act of Aaron is recorded.

egypt.why: Aaron stretched his hand over the waters of Egypt, living and acting there.

babylon.why: Aaron never lives in Babylon or Persia.

jerusalem.why: Aaron never lives or works in Jerusalem.

galilee.why: Aaron never lives or works in Galilee.

sea.why: Aaron never travels by ship.

in-joshua-ruth.why: Aaron appears only in mentions (Joshua 21:4, Judges 20:28), not acting in those events.

in-samuel-kings.why: Aaron is only recalled in 1 Samuel 12:6,8, not acting in those events.

in-chronicles.why: Aaron is only listed in genealogies and priestly references in Chronicles.

in-ezra-esther.why: Aaron appears only in Ezra's genealogy, not acting in the events.

in-prophets.why: Aaron is only mentioned in Micah 6:4 as one sent by God.

in-poetry.why: Aaron is only named in Psalms as part of Israel's history.

in-gospels.why: Aaron appears only as an ancestor in Luke 1:5, not acting.

in-letters.why: Aaron is only mentioned in Hebrews as a priestly type, not writing or receiving.

era-divided.why: Saul and his sons die together in one day, before the kingdom divides.

queen.why: Saul is a man and is never a queen.

high-priest.why: Nothing gives Saul a priestly office; priests act separately in the text.

warrior.why: He organizes the troops into three divisions and leads them against the Ammonites.

court-official.why: He is the king himself; no text has him serving under a king.

shepherd.why: Saul works with oxen and searches for donkeys; no sheep keeping is shown.

fisherman.why: No fishing appears in his story.

twin.why: Twin birth is not stated anywhere in the text.

famous-sibling.why: No brother or sister of Saul appears in the text.

name-changed.why: Saul keeps his name throughout; no new name is given to him.

miracle-birth.why: His mother and any years of barrenness are not described.

long-life.why: Age at death is not stated; he is 30 at the start of a 42-year reign.

miracles.why: No miracle is worked through Saul in the text.

raised.why: Saul dies and is not raised; the spirit at Endor is Samuel's, not Saul's.

taken-up.why: Saul dies in battle and is buried; he is not taken up.

angel.why: No angel speaks to Saul in the text.

dream.why: God does not answer Saul by dreams, Urim or prophets.

interpret-dreams.why: Saul never explains the meaning of a dream.

prison.why: Saul takes Agag captive; he is not imprisoned or carried off himself.

killed.why: He falls on his own sword; an Amalekite claims to have killed him (2 Samuel 1:10).

leader.why: He reigned over all Israel for forty-two years.

battle.why: Saul and his troops march to battle and fight the Philistines.

betrayed.why: Hostility to David and Jonathan is not clearly a betrayal of someone close.

anointed.why: Samuel anoints him with oil as king over Israel.

built.why: He builds a minor altar; it is not a famous structure.

animal.why: The lost donkeys start his story, but the animal is not its centre.

water-miracle.why: No crossing of a sea or river on dry ground, and no walking on water.

song.why: No psalm or song is credited to Saul.

young.why: He is called a young man in 1 Samuel 9:2, but no youthful act is clearly marked.

egypt.why: Saul campaigns near Egypt but does not live or work there.

babylon.why: No time in Babylon or Persia appears in his story.

jerusalem.why: Saul's base is Gibeah; no time in Jerusalem is shown.

galilee.why: No life or work in Galilee appears in his story.

sea.why: No journey by ship appears in his story.

in-prophets.why: Named only in Isaiah 10:29 as a place name; he takes no part.

in-poetry.why: Named only in psalm headings; he is not an actor in Psalms.

queen.why: Abraham is a patriarch; no queen role is given to him.

prophet.why: God calls Abraham a prophet who will pray for Abimelech.

high-priest.why: Melchizedek is the priest in Genesis 14; Abraham is not a high priest.

warrior.why: He armed 318 trained men and pursued the four kings in battle.

levite.why: Lived before Levi's line; no verse states his tribe.

court-official.why: No text places him as an official or servant at a king's court.

shepherd.why: Abram was wealthy in livestock, keeping flocks and herds.

fisherman.why: No fishing in his story.

twin.why: Scripture gives no account of his birth; silence leaves it open.

name-changed.why: God renamed Abram as Abraham.

miracle-birth.why: His mother is not named or described; the text does not say.

long-life.why: Abraham lived a total of 175 years.

tribe-judah.why: Lived before the tribes; no verse states his tribe.

tribe-benjamin.why: Lived before the tribes; no verse states his tribe.

raised.why: He died and was buried; no return to life.

taken-up.why: He breathed his last and died, then was gathered to his people.

angel.why: The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven.

dream.why: The word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision.

interpret-dreams.why: No dream interpretation by Abraham appears in the text.

prison.why: Abraham himself was never imprisoned or carried off; Lot was taken.

killed.why: He died at a ripe old age, not killed by others.

battle.why: He divided his men and struck the kings by night.

enemy.why: He never opposed or attacked God's people.

betrayed.why: Presenting Sarah as his sister may or may not count as denying someone close.

anointed.why: No anointing of Abraham is recorded.

built.why: He built an altar at Shechem where the LORD appeared to him.

animal.why: The ram is a substitute sacrifice, not the animal at the story's centre.

water-miracle.why: No crossing of water by miracle or walking on water.

song.why: No psalm or song is credited to Abraham.

young.why: No deed from his childhood or youth is recorded.

egypt.why: He went down to Egypt to live there during the famine.

babylon.why: Born in Ur of the Chaldeans, but whether that counts as Babylon is open.

jerusalem.why: He lived in Haran, Canaan, Hebron and Gerar; no Jerusalem residence.

galilee.why: No time in Galilee is recorded.

sea.why: No journey by ship is recorded.

in-law.why: Named in Exodus to Deuteronomy only as the covenant patriarch, not acting.

in-joshua-ruth.why: Joshua 24:3 recalls him; he does not act in Joshua's events.

in-samuel-kings.why: Only mentioned in Kings; no acting part.

in-1-kings.why: Only named in Elijah's prayer; no acting part.

in-2-kings.why: Named only in a covenant reference, not in the events.

in-chronicles.why: Named in genealogy and prayers; no acting part.

in-ezra-esther.why: Only recalled in Nehemiah 9:7; no acting part.

in-prophets.why: Only named in Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Micah, not acting.

in-poetry.why: Named in Psalms as a covenant figure; no words credited to him.

in-letters.why: Discussed in Romans and Galatians; not writing, receiving or greeted.

era-judges.why: Solomon's story is told wholly in the United Monarchy, after Saul and David.

era-divided.why: Solomon reigned over the united kingdom and died before the division under Rehoboam.

queen.why: Solomon is a king, not a queen.

high-priest.why: Zadok is the priest anointed with Solomon; Solomon is not shown serving as high priest.

court-official.why: Solomon is the king himself, not an official serving a king.

shepherd.why: No shepherding is described in his story.

fisherman.why: No fishing is described in his story.

twin.why: Twin birth is not mentioned.

name-changed.why: Nathan, sent by the LORD, named him Jedidiah, a new name.

long-life.why: His age at death is not given.

miracles.why: Fire came down from heaven and the glory filled the temple when Solomon finished praying.

raised.why: He died and was buried; no return to life is recorded.

taken-up.why: He died and was buried in the city of David.

angel.why: God speaks to him directly; no angel is shown speaking to him.

dream.why: The LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon.

interpret-dreams.why: No dream interpretation by Solomon is recorded.

prison.why: He is never imprisoned or taken captive.

killed.why: He died in old age and was buried; he was not killed.

leader.why: King Solomon ruled over all Israel.

anointed.why: He was anointed before the LORD as ruler.

built.why: Solomon built the temple and finished it.

animal.why: No story of his centres on an animal.

water-miracle.why: No crossing of water on dry ground or walking on water is recorded.

song.why: The Song of Songs is titled as Solomon's.

young.why: He calls himself young at Gibeon, but his age in the wisdom request is not stated.

egypt.why: He married Pharaoh's daughter but is not shown living or working in Egypt.

babylon.why: No time in Babylon or Persia is recorded.

jerusalem.why: He brought Pharaoh's daughter to the City of David while building his palace in Jerusalem.

galilee.why: No time in Galilee is recorded for him.

sea.why: He owned a fleet with Hiram's sailors, but his own sea travel is not stated.

in-2-kings.why: Named only in 2 Kings as a past builder, not taking part in its events.

in-ezra-esther.why: Named only, as the source of servants and as a past sinner.

in-prophets.why: Mentioned in Jeremiah only, as a past builder.

in-poetry.why: The proverbs are credited to Solomon son of David.

in-gospels.why: Named only, as Jesus' comparison and a place name, not acting in the events.

book-named.why: No book is named for him; the Song is credited to him but not titled by him alone.

ruler.why: Ruled Egypt only under Pharaoh; Pharaoh alone is king.

ruler-israel.why: Never king of Israel or Judah; he served under Pharaoh in Egypt.

ruler-foreign.why: ruler is no

queen.why: A man; never a queen or a king's wife.

high-priest.why: Not a high priest; Potiphera the priest of On is Asenath's father.

warrior.why: No military role; his service was administrative and in the grain supply.

levite.why: Joseph's descendants are the tribes of Manasseh and Ephraim, not Levi.

court-official.why: Entered Pharaoh's service and was placed over all Egypt.

shepherd.why: Was tending the flock with his brothers at seventeen.

fisherman.why: No fishing in his story.

twin.why: Born to Rachel first; no verse states whether he had a twin.

name-changed.why: Pharaoh gave him the name Zaphenath-paneah.

miracle-birth.why: Rachel was barren until God opened her womb and she bore Joseph.

long-life.why: Scripture says he died at the age of 110.

miracles.why: No miracle is recorded as done through Joseph; he interprets dreams.

raised.why: No death and return to life in his story.

taken-up.why: He died and was embalmed in Egypt.

angel.why: No angel speaks to Joseph in his story.

dream.why: He has dreams, but the text does not say God sent his own dreams.

interpret-dreams.why: Explains the meaning of Pharaoh's dreams of the coming years.

prison.why: Thrown into the prison where the king's prisoners were confined.

killed.why: Sold into Egypt and died of age; not killed by others.

leader.why: Lord of Egypt under Pharaoh; not leader of God's people as a nation.

battle.why: No battle is recorded in his story.

enemy.why: He did not oppose or attack Israel; his brothers plotted against him.

betrayed.why: He was betrayed by his brothers; he betrayed no one close to him.

anointed.why: No anointing with oil is recorded for him.

built.why: No famous structure is recorded as built by him.

animal.why: Animals appear only in passing; no animal is the centre of his story.

water-miracle.why: No crossing of water on dry ground or walking on water.

song.why: No psalm or song is credited to him by name.

young.why: At seventeen he brought his father a bad report and told his dreams.
